## What Has the Solver Actually Established?

A feasible numerical optimization result is meaningful only relative to its constraints, tolerances and domain. Failure can mean an inadequate metric family, numerical trouble or actual infeasibility; it does not by itself prove the system cannot be stabilized.

## A Precise LTI Program

For $\dot x=Ax+Bu$, negative feedback $u=-Kx$, and fixed desired rate $\lambda>0$, seek $M\succ0$ with

$$
(A-BK)^\top M+M(A-BK)+2\lambda M\preceq0.
$$

This is bilinear in $M,K$. With $X=M^{-1}$ and $Y=KX$, congruence gives the LMI

$$
\begin{gathered}
AX+XA^\top-BY\\
-Y^\top B^\top+2\lambda X\preceq0,\qquad X\succ0.
\end{gathered}
$$

Recover $K=YX^{-1}$. The rate is fixed for this convex feasibility problem; optimizing $\lambda X$ jointly is not an LMI. Test candidate rates separately, and verify residuals and conditioning after numerical recovery [@boyd1994].

## Continuous and Discrete Residuals Differ

For a continuous closed-loop field, evaluate $R=A^\top M+MA+\dot M+2\lambda M$, with the total derivative along that field. For a discrete map $F_k$, put $A_{c,k}=DF_k(x)$ and $M^+=M(F_k(x),k+1)$. Evaluate

$$
\begin{aligned}
R_k(x)&=A_{c,k}^\top M^+A_{c,k}-\rho M(x,k),\\
&\qquad 0<\rho<1.
\end{aligned}
$$

Do not substitute sampled-map Jacobians into a continuous-time inequality. Feedback derivatives, actuator saturation and additional states must match the implementation.

## Samples Are Evidence, Not Coverage

The scalar field $f(x)=x-\tfrac43x^3$ has $f'(\pm1)=-3$ and $f'(0)=1$. Endpoint checks miss an expanding interior. Monte Carlo rollouts likewise cannot exclude unsampled failures.

A coverage argument can bridge the gap: if a symmetric residual is Lipschitz with a validated constant $L$, every point lies within radius $r$ of a sample, and each sampled residual satisfies $R_i\preceq-\mu I$, then $Lr<\mu$ preserves negativity throughout the covered set. Numerical error must be included in the margin; metric definiteness and invariance remain separate requirements.

Control contraction metric synthesis also requires conditions for constructing a finite controller from differential feedback. The original theorem's integrability amendment is relevant when input rank changes [@manchester2017ccm; @manchester2017amendment]. A trajectory-wise gain or sampled inequality alone does not establish that theorem's hypotheses.
